entries.english:
We, Wok von Rosenberg, in our own name and that of our brothers and heirs, declare by this letter publicly and before everyone who sees it or hears it read that the reverend priest Johann, pastor of the Rosenberg church and our dear chaplain, appeared before us and explained that he pays rents and lodgings from his lands and meadows to our chamber, to the prudent mayor and council, and to all the community of our city of Rosenberg. He humbly asked us graciously to free those lands and meadows from such rents, dues, and lodgings, so that divine worship might be increased. The lands and meadows are listed here, together with what is paid from them: eight denarii from a plot on Galingberg; sixteen denarii from other fields, three lussels and one plot by Krpcz’s clearing above Wachterbach; one florin from two little meadows outside the outer mill, one above and one below the road; seventeen denarii from the meadow by Winkcheltar; eight denarii from the plot at Partlem; two pfennigs from a little garden by the Wulta at Guschlen; three groschen from the plot at Melczen by the Schawrgraben; and thirteen pfennigs from three lussels on Galingberg belonging to Caspar.

Taking the pastor’s humble and proper request into account, and mindful of the divine gifts with which God’s grace has abundantly favored us, and wishing to honor His holy grace from our estate and further increase the honor and praise of God celebrated at the said church, we have carefully and deliberately freed, and by this letter definitively and fully free, the above lands and meadows from the rents and dues owed to us and from all customary lodgings owed to our townspeople of Rosenberg. We do so with the unanimous consent and goodwill of those who have traditionally received these dues at our request and intercession. Accordingly, neither the present pastor nor any future pastors of Rosenberg shall ever owe us, our heirs and successors, or the present or future townspeople of Rosenberg any rents, lodgings, payments, or other dues from these lands, but may hold and enjoy them freely, without hindrance or disturbance. In return for this benefaction and freedom of the said lands, the pastor of Rosenberg has agreed and promised, for himself and all future pastors, that each year during the octave of All Saints’ Day, without omission or delay, they will hold a memorial service with ten priests for all the former lords of Rosenberg, for us, and for all our heirs and successors. In confirmation, we have ordered our own seal attached to this letter. Given at Krumau on Friday, Saint Dorothy’s Day, in the year 1489.

The seal hangs from a parchment strip in red wax; it is damaged and has been described above.
